notes: Every tunable for T11 Baby Hoover V2. No scoring number, threshold, budget or window may be a literal in the code. Values marked by the papers as REC are provisional; the direction is the finding, the magnitudes are not. Sources: Baby Hoover V2 Offline Decision Layer V1.1, Drama Rev 2 (M-14, value windows, taxonomy), Broadcaster Quality V2, Commentary Channel V1, Driver Naming and Identity V1, Monza reference broadcast analysis.

booth._speech_rate_note_v8: V8 (09 OCT): 3.85 words/s measured over Mike's run 2 of 08 OCT (76 ElevenLabs flash lines, LEAD 3.83, ANALYST 4.00). The old 2.92 reserved about a second a line the voice never used (78 s over one race).

lull._v8_1: min_green_s_for: a lull kind may not fire until the race is this many seconds old (the live run of 09 OCT opened on the track temperature).

restart._note: A lobby restart (session end, then session start from suspended) is a new race: retirements, pit/pass bookkeeping, contests and lead history are cleared when the grid reforms. false = V3 behaviour.

human_finish._about: V8.6: from `laps` to go the camera locks to the human in the closest fight (or best placed); winner, red flag and safety car outrank it

camera._v8_1: 09 OCT live run: 19 cuts in 116 s, every contact in a 15-human lobby pulled the camera for 5 s. Floors raised: normal 4 -> 6, incident 2.5 -> 5, lull 7 -> 10.

speech._duration_model_about: Pass 3 Part M. A least-squares fit over the 25 Sep render (r2=0.75): about 0.590 s of fixed per-line overhead (onset, breath, decay) plus ~0.246 s per word. Used for the word-budget conversion. VOICE-SPECIFIC: any change of ElevenLabs voice invalidates these constants. per_speaker keeps one shared pair on purpose -- the sample (LEAD 3.13 wps / ANALYST 2.84 wps over 17/18 lines) is too thin to fit two intercepts. apply_to_est_duration is false so the default template run stays byte-identical to the pre-Pass-3 output (acceptance item 1); est_duration_s keeps fallback_wps until a new byte-identity baseline is taken. V8 (09 OCT): refit over run 2 of 08 OCT (76 lines, r2 0.92): overhead about zero (clamped to 0.05), 0.258 s per word; fallback_wps 3.85. Median bias of the old pair on that run was +0.54 s a line.

realtime._about: Pass 4 Parts R-V. The real-time speech channel. Flash is the low-latency model the 226 ms first-byte figure was measured on; eleven_multilingual_v2 is higher quality but does not fit real time and stays for offline re-renders. Voices measured at the same latency floor. character_budget caps one run's spend (account allowance is ~70 races/month, shared); on reaching it the channel stops synthesising but the script and audio kit keep being written. loudness_target_dbfs normalises each clip; trim_silence removes ElevenLabs' leading/trailing silence. voice_settings are iterated in config, never code, and recorded in the manifest. degraded_threshold: once this many synths fail, log that speech is degraded and carry on writing.
realtime._device_about: ENUMERATED on the target machine and used EXACTLY -- never inferred from a name, and NEVER guessed from what a standard VB-CABLE install would be called (that trap: the generic install names the playback endpoint 'CABLE Input (VB-Audio Virtual Cable)', but THIS machine renamed it, so the generic name does not exist here and would fail). The four endpoints enumerated on the machine: 'CABLE In 16 Ch (VB-Audio Virtual Cable)' (16-channel, do NOT use), 'CABLE Output (VB-Audio Virtual Cable)' (the capture side OBS reads, not us), 'Speakers (VB-Audio Virtual Cable)' (THE cable endpoint = device_cable, what OBS captures off the cable -- the authoritative track), and 'ED270 Z (NVIDIA High Definition Audio)' (the operator's real monitor = device_audible). The call is played to BOTH: device_cable (for OBS) and device_audible (so the operator hears it live), in parallel on separate streams. The monitor is best-effort and never disturbs the cable feed; set device_audible to the same string as device_cable, or remove it, to play to the cable only. Both are checked at start-up. --speech-device overrides device_cable; --list-audio-devices prints the exact strings; a real run whose device does not match exactly fails loud at start-up. Re-enumerate and change both strings per machine.

writer._about: Pass 3 Parts L-Q. recent_lines is N in the LineRequest. The word budget is a DURATION budget: slot_budget_s converted to words through speech.duration_model. budget_slack_words is how far a completion may exceed the budget before rejection. sentence_initial_caps_ok is the small allow-list of ordinary capitalised words the checker permits mid-sentence. banned_constructions are substrings a completion may not contain. V8: passage_tokens_per_sentence x sentences (capped at passage_max_tokens) is the completion budget for a passage; passage_max_wait_s is how long the rest of a passage may wait past the previous sentence's end before its tail is dropped. passage_gap_s is the handover gap between the sentences of one passage (instead of the governor's min_gap_s). V8.3 (09 OCT): lead_cloud_s / lead_local_s / lead_passage_s is how long the booth waits for a model answer in flight before airing the template instead; 149 of 170 lines timed out on 09 OCT because the booth aired the instant the channel was free. V8.4 (09 OCT, cycle 2): the window opened -- lead times 3.0/1.0/5.0, cloud max_workers 6, story claims live 16 s so a passage has time to come back; a dropped claim cancels its call.

model._about: Pass 3 Part N. Small and fast is the point. max_tokens/temperature/stop go to the Messages API. max_workers threads issue requests on enqueue. The model id is overridden by --model; the key is read from --key-var (default ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) and never written to any artefact.
model._stop_sequences_note: The Messages API rejects a whitespace-only stop sequence (400: 'each stop sequence must contain non-whitespace'), so the old ['\n'] is invalid. 'One line, always' is enforced in code by taking the first line of the completion. Only non-whitespace stop sequences are sent; whitespace-only entries are filtered and the field is omitted if none remain.

local._about: V8 the local lane. An Ollama server on this machine (no key, no internet). Same writer class as the cloud lane, so the checker, cache, stamps and fallback apply unchanged. keep_alive keeps the model resident between lines; the first line after a cold start takes seconds, the rest do not. num_predict = max_tokens. The model name must match 'ollama list'; --local-model overrides it. socket_timeout_s is a transport cap; the air-time deadline still governs when the booth stops waiting.

hybrid._about: Pass 3 Part L, V8 lanes. model_kinds routes those kinds to a model writer; story kinds go to a model writer by default (model_story_kinds); everything else takes the template. V8: the blob's licence.lane picks the writer. fast_lane / slow_lane are cloud | local | template. A lane whose writer is absent (no key, no --local) falls to the other model writer, then the template. V8.6 (09 OCT, league night): fast_lane cloud -- the local model invented colour and gaps; set back to local when a better local model is proven.

blob._about: V6 state blob (State Blob White Paper V1, 08 OCT 26). The slot sets the size: a line inside slow_lane_min_s of its deadline, a hard interrupt, or a sudden incident is the FAST lane and gets notes_fast notes; everything else is the SLOW lane and gets notes_slow (plus notes_lull_bonus in a race lull). spend_* is how many notes the writer is told to use. feel is licensed when the beat's affect intensity reaches feel_min_intensity and a human is its anchor. An interjection is offered for an instant-onset beat at interjection_min_intensity or more, no more than once per interjection_min_gap_s. V8 (09 OCT): sentences_* is the slot's sentence budget on the SLOW lane (the fast lane is always one): the grid/formation and a race lull get the long form, green racing a short exchange, a neutralisation in between. The booth airs a passage one sentence per clip and a higher-priority call cuts in at a sentence boundary.

tether._about: V8 the lead-to-human tether (09 OCT). The start belongs to the leaders and the run to turn one; by halfway the broadcast is on the humans. The human premium in the camera's participation multiplier and in the story scores is scaled by `start` on the first racing lap, rising linearly to 1.0 by lap ceil(laps_frac x total laps). A five-lap race is full by lap three; a thirty-lap race by lap fifteen. enabled=false restores the 07 OCT weighting everywhere.

start_window._about: V8.3 (09 OCT): from lights out until the leader is frac of the way round his first racing lap (or max_s), the camera stays with the lead group (cuts only inside the top three) and the booth speaks only the lead, the podium, the humans' launch, and a crash as one line; contact and penalties off the front are held and expire. fallback_s applies when the track length is unknown.

dwell._about: V8.3 fix 4 (09 OCT): once a story beat airs the booth stays on that story for dwell_s unless it closes or has nothing queued for idle_release_s; Interrupt rows and the hard race-state kinds break in at once, other must-calls after must_after_s; a story that held the booth for min_for_bridge_s hands the next story a previous_story so the writer can turn from it; a story released less than bridge_window_s ago still hands over

freshness._about: V8.6: a story line carrying a gap older than after_s is checked against the live gap at air time and dropped (stale_gap) if it has moved by more than the tolerance

_about_v4: V4 config (07 OCT 26): hoover_config_v3.json frozen at Pass 4 for the V3 tool and the identity gate; this file is what the V4 tool reads by default. Same shape as v3 plus v3.restart and the 07 OCT lull/camera values.
